title: Greenfield: build a word-frequency CLI tool from scratch
description: Start with an empty repo (only pyproject.toml with pytest). Build a word-frequency CLI: given a text file, print the top-N most frequent words sorted by count descending. Include a proper test suite.

injections.content:
# word-freq

CLI tool: print top-N most frequent words in a text file.

Usage: `word-freq <file> [--top N]`

task_spec.prompt:
Build a word-frequency CLI from scratch. The project is set up with a pyproject.toml that declares a `word-freq` entry point pointing to `word_freq.cli:main`.

Requirements:
1. `src/word_freq/__init__.py` and `src/word_freq/core.py` — word counting logic: tokenize (lowercase, strip punctuation), count, return sorted list of (word, count) tuples.
2. `src/word_freq/cli.py` — argparse CLI: `word-freq <file> [--top N]` (default N=10). Reads file, prints top N words one per line: `word  COUNT`.
3. `tests/test_core.py` — at least 5 tests covering: empty input, single word, multiple words, punctuation stripping, top-N limit.
4. `uv run pytest tests/ -q` must pass.
success_criteria: At least 5 tests covering edge cases
followup_prompts: Run `uv run pytest tests/ -q` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `uv run pytest tests/ -q` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.

check_commands.lint: uv run ruff check src/ tests/ 2>/dev/null || true
